This petition is filed by husband and in-laws seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.2769/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 506, 498A, 504 and 323 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. Today, a joint affidavit is placed on record, duly signed by the first petitioner-husband, his family members (in- laws), and the second respondent-wife.

In the said affidavit, it is unequivocally stated that the marriage between the first NC: 2025:KHC:35113 HC-KAR petitioner and the second respondent has already been dissolved by mutual consent before the competent Family Court.
It is further stated that subsequent to the dissolution of marriage, the second respondent has entered into a fresh marriage and is presently leading her matrimonial life with her second husband.
At paragraph No.4 of the joint affidavit, the second respondent has also disclosed that she is expecting a child from her second husband.
3. The second respondent-complainant is personally present before this Court and acknowledges the factum of dissolution of marriage with the first petitioner.
She also affirms before this Court that she has remarried and is leading a settled life.

In view of the amicable settlement arrived at between the Sri Santhosh R vs The State Of Karnataka By on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147437570/
2 parties and on a specific query made by this Court, the second respondent has reiterated her willingness to put an end to the present criminal proceedings and has no objection if the same are quashed.
4.

sentences.text: This Court is conscious of the fact that the offence punishable under Section 498-A of the IPC is not compoundable.
However,

having regard to the peculiar facts NC: 2025:KHC:35113 HC-KAR and circumstances of the present case, namely, that the matrimonial relationship between the parties has already come to an end by way of a of divorce, that the second respondent has since remarried and is now expecting a child from her second husband, and that she has expressed her desire not to pursue the criminal case any further, this Court is of the considered opinion that the continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.

In order to secure the ends of justice, this Court finds it just and appropriate to exercise its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
to give a quietus to the dispute.

5. Recording the presence of the second respondent- complainant and her statement undertaking to withdraw all allegations made against the petitioners, the proceedings in C.C. No.2769/2024 are hereby quashed.
Accordingly, the criminal petition stands disposed of.
